newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Van den Broek denies confusion on enlargement.
newsitem.headline: Van den Broek denies confusion on enlargement.

text.p: Commissioner Hans van den Broek denied on Thursday there was any confusion over the timetable for admitting new members from central and eastern Europe to the European Union.

The Commission said in a fact sheet on Wednesday that the earliest realistic date for new admissions was 2002 but then backtracked, saying this did not represent the official stance of the EU executive.

Asked if he thought applicants would now be disppointed or confused, Van den Broek said: "If they are disappointed, they are certainly not confused because they know exactly what we are talking about."
The Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland are seen as the leading contenders of 10 central and east European countries seeking EU membership.
Van den Broek, the commissioner responsible for relations with central and eastern Europe, said the issue was not if, but when, the applicants would become members.

"The when is solely determined by the degree of preparation that the countries will have reached and the time it will need to ratify the results of the negotiations," he told a meeting on the first day of a visit to Prague.
Talks on EU expansion are due to begin six months after the end, scheduled in June, of the EU inter-governmental conference.
